ai.literal: With milk honey having mixed is just like that, of the gentle-speeched one's white teeth welled-up water.
ai.translation: The moisture that wells up from the bright teeth of this woman of gentle speech is like a sweet mixture of milk and honey.
ai.modern: பாலோடு தேன் கலந்தது போன்றது, மென்மையான சொற்களைப் பேசும் இவளுடைய வெண்மையான பற்களிலிருந்து சுரக்கும் நீர்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the lover praises the sweetness of his beloved. He compares the moisture or saliva from her mouth to a delicious mixture of milk and honey. The term 'பணிமொழி' describes her gentle and soft speech, while 'வாலெயிறு' refers to her bright, white teeth. By comparing the moisture from her teeth to milk and honey, the poet conveys the intense pleasure and sweetness the lover experiences in her presence.

ai.literal: With the body, the soul, between, what kind of [bond], then, like that, with the young woman, my, between, the love.
ai.translation: The love between this young woman and me is just like the inseparable bond that exists between the body and the soul.
ai.modern: உடம்புக்கும் உயிருக்கும் இடையே உள்ள உறவு எத்தகையதோ, அத்தகையதே இந்த இளம் பெண்ணுக்கும் எனக்கும் இடையே உள்ள காதல் உறவு ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully illustrates the depth of love by comparing it to the relationship between the physical body and the life-giving soul. The words 'உடம்பொடு' (with the body) and 'உயிர்' (soul) represent two distinct entities that cannot exist without each other. The phrase 'என்ன மற்று அன்ன' sets up the comparison, meaning 'just as that is, so is this'. By describing their 'நட்பு' (which here means intimate love) in this manner, the speaker emphasizes that their connection is not merely physical or temporary, but vital to their very existence.

words.gloss: for the one with a beautiful forehead

ai.literal: In the black pupil, O image, you go away; for the one with a beautiful forehead whom I desire, there is no space.
ai.translation: O image in the pupil of my eye, please leave! There is no room here for my beloved of the beautiful forehead whom I adore.
ai.modern: என் கண்ணின் கருமணியில் இருக்கும் பாவையே! நீ வெளியேறிவிடு. நான் விரும்பும் அழகிய நெற்றியை உடைய என் காதலி அமர்வதற்கு இங்கே இடமில்லை.
ai.explanation: The lover playfully addresses the tiny reflection or pupil-image (pāvāi) in his own eye. He asks this image to leave (pōthāy) because he wants his beloved, who has a beautiful forehead (tirunutal), to enter and reside in his eyes. Since the pupil is already occupied by the reflection, he claims there is no room (illai iṭam) for her. This poetic conceit beautifully illustrates how the lover wishes to keep his beloved constantly in his sight and heart.

ai.literal: Living is like to life she of choice jewels; dying is like to that when she departs.
ai.translation: She who wears choice jewels is like life itself when she is with me; when she departs, she is like death.
ai.modern: தேர்ந்தெடுத்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த இவள் என்னோடு இருக்கும்போது உயிருக்கு வாழ்தல் போன்றவள்; என்னை விட்டுப் பிரியும்போது அதற்குச் சாதல் போன்றவள்.
ai.explanation: The hero describes the intense impact his beloved has on his existence. When she is near, her presence is as vital and joyful as life itself. However, the moment she departs, the separation feels as painful and destructive as death. By comparing her presence to life and her absence to death, the couplet illustrates the absolute dependence of the lover's soul on his beloved.

ai.translation: I would think of her if I ever forgot her; but I do not know what it is to forget the qualities of my beloved with bright, beautiful eyes.
ai.modern: ஒளிபொருந்திய அழகிய கண்களை உடையவளின் நற்குணங்களை நான் மறந்தால் அல்லவா நினைக்க வேண்டும்? நான் அவளை மறப்பதையே அறியமாட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The lover expresses the depth of his constant devotion by playing on the concepts of remembering and forgetting. He states that he would only need to actively recall his beloved if he had first forgotten her. However, because the qualities of his beloved, who has bright and beautiful eyes, never leave his mind, he does not even know what it means to forget her. Thus, constant remembrance makes active recollection unnecessary.

ai.literal: From within (my) eye, (he) does not depart; if (I) blink, will (he) suffer pain? Subtle is my lover.
ai.translation: My lover does not depart from within my eyes; if I blink, will he suffer pain? So subtle is his form.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என் கண்ணின் உள்ளிருந்து வெளியே போக மாட்டார்; நான் கண்ணிமைத்தால் அவர் துன்புறுவாரோ? என் காதலர் அவ்வளவு நுட்பமானவர்.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses her deep love by imagining her lover residing permanently inside her eyes. She says he never leaves this inner sanctuary. Because he is so delicate and subtle in form, she worries that the simple act of blinking her eyes might squeeze or hurt him. This poetic imagery beautifully illustrates how constantly and intimately her lover occupies her vision and thoughts.

words.gloss: He who is inside the eyes

ai.literal: Since the beloved is inside the eyes, even the eyes we will not paint, knowing that he would be hidden.
ai.translation: Since my beloved resides within my eyes, I will not even paint them with kohl, knowing that doing so would hide him from my view.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என் கண்ணுக்குள்ளே இருப்பதால், மை எழுதும்போது கண் மூடுவதால் அவர் மறைந்துவிடுவார் என்பதை அறிந்து, நான் என் கண்களுக்கு மை கூட எழுத மாட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the heroine expresses her intense and constant love. She says her lover resides permanently inside her eyes. Therefore, she refuses to apply kohl (eye-paint) to her eyes, knowing that the act of applying it would require closing her eyes, which would temporarily hide him from her inner sight. This poetic exaggeration highlights how she cannot bear to lose sight of her beloved even for a single moment.

ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully illustrates the depth of the heroine's love through a tender, imaginative fear. She believes her lover physically resides inside her heart. Consequently, she fears eating hot food because she knows the heat might burn him. This hyperbolic expression shows how her thoughts are entirely consumed by her beloved, to the extent that even her basic daily actions are performed with his comfort in mind.

ai.literal: If [I] blink, [his] hiding I know; just for that, 'stranger' says this town.
ai.translation: I know that if I blink, my lover who lives in my eyes will be hidden from me; yet, just because I do not blink to avoid this, the people of this town call him an unkind stranger.
ai.modern: நான் கண் இமைத்தால் என் கண்ணுக்குள் இருக்கும் காதலர் மறைந்துவிடுவார் என்பதை நான் அறிவேன்; அவ்வாறு இமைக்காமல் இருப்பதைக் கண்டு, இந்த ஊர் மக்கள் அவரை அன்பில்லாதவர் என்று தூற்றுகின்றனர்.
ai.explanation: The heroine explains that her lover is always present inside her eyes. She avoids blinking because she knows that even a momentary blink would hide him from her sight. However, the ignorant villagers do not understand this sweet secret; seeing her unblinking, tearful, or strained eyes, they gossip and call her lover an unsympathetic stranger who does not care for her. The word 'karappākku' refers to the hiding of her lover, and 'ētilar' highlights the town's lack of understanding, as they mistake her loving vigilance for distress caused by an uncaring partner.

ai.literal: Rejoicingly he dwells within my heart always; (yet) 'he dwells having departed, he is a stranger,' says this town.
ai.translation: My beloved dwells forever joyfully within my heart; yet the people of this town gossip that he has abandoned me and is a stranger.
ai.modern: அவர் எப்போதும் என் மனதிற்குள் மகிழ்ச்சியோடு வாழ்கிறார்; ஆனால், இந்த ஊர் மக்கள் அவர் என்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்றுவிட்டார், அவர் எனக்கு அந்நியர் என்று சொல்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The heroine describes the contrast between her inner experience of love and the outer world's perception. Though her lover has physically traveled away, she feels his presence constantly and joyfully inside her heart. However, the townspeople, who can only see his physical absence, gossip that he has deserted her and call him an uncaring stranger. This couplet beautifully highlights how true love transcends physical distance, making the beloved ever-present to the mind.
